name: Indus Towers Ltd
title: Indus Towers Ltd - 534816 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 tower adds ~3,100 with tenancy ratio flat at 1.62 but incremental tenancy ratio ~1.3-1.4; EBITDA +3% YoY, energy margin -4.6%, management offers no numeric guidance beyond a 3-4 quarter order book.

summary.headline: Indus Towers Q1 FY27 gross revenue rose 4.6% YoY to INR 84.3 bn; EBITDA up 3.0% to INR 45.2 bn, margin 53.6%.
summary.overview: Gross revenue grew 4.6% YoY to INR 84.3 bn, with core rental up 5.2% YoY to INR 53.7 bn on tower and colocation additions. Reported EBITDA rose 3.0% YoY to INR 45.2 bn, but margin fell 1.5 pp YoY to 53.6%; adjusting for a prior-year INR 0.9 bn write-back, EBITDA grew 5.2%. Energy margin was -4.6% (seasonal, plus past-period settlements), while diesel consumption fell 13% YoY. Management reiterated a firm order book for 3-4 quarters and began Africa rollouts guidance for next quarter, with economics still undisclosed. The CFO also announced his departure after five years.

financial_highlights.change: +3.0% YoY (+5.2% adjusted for prior-year INR 0.9 bn write-back); +1.2% QoQ

segments.name: India towers (macro)
segments.commentary: Added about 3,100 macro towers, taking base to about 267,600 (+6.3% YoY); tenancy ratio stable at 1.62. Including lean towers, about 446,300 towers.

segments.name: Colocations
segments.commentary: Added about 4,200 colocations, taking base to about 432,300 (+5.1% YoY). Incremental tenancy ratio about 1.3-1.4 over the last 2-4 quarters.

segments.name: Energy
segments.commentary: Energy revenue rose 9.5% QoQ on seasonal diesel use and higher diesel prices; diesel consumption down over 13% YoY; solar access on about 46,000 sites (about 3,700 added); solar installed base 259 MW.

segments.name: Africa
segments.commentary: Licences and regulatory approvals received in Nigeria, Uganda and Zambia; anchor-customer orders secured; rollouts to start next quarter. No financials disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Management cites a firm order book for the next 3-4 quarters, irrespective of customer funding.
Tower supply constraint from West Asia/LPG disruption said to be resolved; no supply-chain constraint on tower growth expected in Q2, though battery supplies expected to recover from August.
Monsoon may slow growth in some states in Q2.
Africa rollouts to commence next quarter (Q2) and scale progressively; tenancy and unit-economics disclosure deferred until material.
Management expects colocation additions to keep outpacing tower additions, subject to one customer's capital infusion.
Board committed to distributing free cash flow; Africa capex expected to be moderate and largely debt-funded in initial 1-2 years.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex includes replacement of lead-acid batteries and DG sets; maintenance capex roughly doubled from about INR 250 crore to above INR 500 crore per quarter over five quarters, with moderation expected later.
Battery programme to replace diesel with lithium-ion banks slowed in Q1 by battery supply constraints; expected to pick up in coming quarters.
Launched internal platform to simplify tower design and site planning.
Africa capex expected to be moderate in initial years, largely debt-funded; no figures given.
demand_pricing: 5G BTS installed base at 563,000, up 32,000 in Q1 FY27; TRAI reports 5G subscribers above 427 million.
Total data consumption grew 31% YoY in Q4 FY26; 5G share of traffic 43% vs 30% a year earlier.
Rental growth broadly tracks tower and colocation growth; escalation (about 2.5%) offset by revenue equalisation and renewal discounts; ARPT pressured by lean-design mix and rural additions.
Exits/churn described as business as usual, with no disproportionate churn from any customer.
Management declined to give Vodafone Idea-specific tenancy share, saying Indus is securing the bulk of the rollout plan.

qa_highlights.question: Why are rental revenues growing in line with colocations rather than faster, given escalation?
qa_highlights.answer: Escalation and 5G loading growth are much smaller than tower and colocation additions; renewal discounts and revenue equalisation on towers in years 5-6 offset escalation.

qa_highlights.question: Is Airtel in-sourcing towers a risk to tenancies on existing towers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it executes whatever order book it gets, sees no net tenancy loss from the strategy, and sees Africa anchor tenancy and synergies as value-creating.

qa_highlights.question: Africa unit economics, margin and returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Unit economics, rate cards and MSA still being finalised; management will disclose once rollouts start, and says returns will cover cost of capital even with a single tenant.

qa_highlights.question: Capex per tower looks like about INR 39 lakh versus INR 20-25 lakh standard?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth capex includes replacement, maintenance, solar and battery spend, so dividing total capex by towers added is misleading; offline walkthrough offered.

qa_highlights.question: Why is energy margin under pressure and how do battery investments earn returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Seasonality and past-period settlements drove the energy margin decline; battery capex is recovered through customer payments that replace diesel pass-through, so the revenue continues in a different form.

qa_highlights.question: Why is maintenance capex roughly doubled?
qa_highlights.answer: Replacement of lead-acid batteries and DG sets is driving it; lithium-ion transition to continue for some time before moderation.

risks_watch: Tenancy ratio at 1.62 base vs incremental 1.3-1.4; continued pressure on ARPT and rental growth.
Customer funding and capital raise by Vodafone Idea; possible BSNL tower tie-up was raised but not commented on.
Africa economics undisclosed; margin and return dilution risk unknown until MSA and rate cards are finalised.
Energy margin weakness in H1 due to monsoon-related diesel use; diesel-to-battery transition delayed by battery supply.
Elevated maintenance capex (battery and DG replacement) above prior run-rate.
CFO transition after five years; leadership change to watch.
Possible Airtel stake purchase; management declined to comment.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order book and cash flow, but evasive on Africa unit economics, Airtel intent, customer-level tenancy and the reasons for lower tenancy ratios. Management repeatedly deferred numbers to future quarters.
key_quotes: We have visibility of the order book that is firm for the next 3 to 4 quarters.
So we will be covering the cost of capital even with single tenancy.
Diesel consumption on our sites has seen a reduction of 13% year-on-year in Q1 FY27.
I would not really worry too much about the 1.37 for a couple of quarters.

adds.what: About 3,100 macro towers added in Q1 (base about 267,600, +6.3% YoY)
About 4,200 colocations added in Q1 (base about 432,300, +5.1% YoY)
Africa tower rollouts in Nigeria, Uganda and Zambia; anchor orders secured, no unit count or capex figures disclosed

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; management cites a firm order book for 3-4 quarters and tower supply disruption resolved, with steady ~3,100 macro tower and ~4,200 colocation additions per quarter and Africa rollouts starting next quarter, but Africa economics and tenancy are undisclosed.

mgmt.note: CFO announced departure after five years; no successor plan or growth stance given on the call.
